questions.question: The process of conversion of sugar into alcohol is known as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fermentation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of conversion of **sugar into alcohol** is known as **fermentation.**
 
• Fermentation is a **metabolic process** that converts** sugar to acids, gases, or alcohol.**
 
• The fermentation process is used in food production, such as **bread, cheese, yogurt, and beer.**
 
• In the alcohol industry, fermentation is the first step in the production of **alcoholic beverages.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Denudation** is the process of erosion or stripping away of the earth's surface by natural agents like **water, wind, or ice.**
 
• **Fragmentation** is the breaking up of a larger entity into **smaller pieces.**
 
• **Infiltration** is the movement of water through the** soil surface into the ground.**

questions.question: Sterility is caused due to the deficiency of which of the following Vitamins?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**E.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sterility** is a condition in which an individual is unable to **conceive or produce offspring**, and it can have various causes such as **hormonal imbalances, infections, genetic disorders, and lifestyle factors.**
 
• **Vitamin E** plays a crucial role in maintaining the** reproductive system **and preventing **oxidative damage** to the reproductive cells.
 
• **Vitamin D** is essential for the **absorption of calcium and bone health,** and its deficiency can lead to** rickets, osteoporosis, **and other bone-related disorders.
 
• **Vitamin K** is required for **blood clotting and bone health**, and its deficiency can lead to** bleeding disorders and osteoporosis.**
 
• **Vitamin B1,** also known as** thiamine**, is essential for **carbohydrate metabolism, nerve function, and energy production, **and its deficiency can lead to beriberi and other neurological disorders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vitamin E** is a **fat-soluble vitamin **that is found in** nuts, seeds, vegetable oils, and green leafy vegetables.**
 
• It acts as an antioxidant and protects the cells from **oxidative damage** caused by free radicals.
 
• **Vitamin D** is synthesized in the skin when exposed to sunlight and is also found in **fatty fish, egg yolks, and fortified foods** such as **milk and cereals.**
 
• **Vitamin K **is found in** green leafy vegetables, liver,** and fermented foods such as **cheese and natto.**
 
• **Vitamin B1** is found in** whole grains, legumes, nuts, and meat.**
 
• It is important to maintain a** balanced and varied diet** to ensure adequate intake of all essential **vitamins and minerals.**

questions.question: In pre-independent India, who was the first person to discuss the concept of poverty line?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** was the first person to discuss the **concept of poverty line** in pre-independent India.
 
• He introduced the concept in his book **"Poverty and Un-British Rule in India" **published in **1901.**
 
• Naoroji defined poverty line as the **minimum income required** to meet the basic needs of an individual.
 
• He argued that poverty was not due to the **laziness or incompetence** of the Indian people but was a result of the **economic policies** of the British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahadev Govind Ranade** was a **social reformer and scholar** who advocated for the **upliftment of women and lower castes.**
 
• **B.R. Ambedkar** was a prominent leader of the **Dalit community** and played a key role in **drafting the Indian constitution.**
 
• **M.K. Gandhi** was a leader of the **Indian independence movement** and is known for his **nonviolent civil disobedience tactics.**

questions.question: The concept of "Republic" in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the constitution of which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**France.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **"Republic"** refers to a **form of government** where the head of state is** not** a **monarch,** but a **president **or other elected official.
 
• India adopted the concept of "Republic" in its Constitution on **January 26, 1950**, when it became a **sovereign democratic republic.**
 
• The Constitution of India was largely influenced by the Constitutions of the** United States, the United Kingdom, and France.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Germany** did not have a republican form of government until after **World War II.**
 
• **Australia** became a republic only in **1999, **while India adopted the concept of Republic in 1950.
 
• **Japan **has a **constitutional monarchy,** where the **Emperor** is the** symbolic head of state.**
 
• **France **was the first country to adopt the **Republican form **of government during the **French Revolution in 1792.**

questions.question: In which year was All-India Muslim League formed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1906.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** All-India Muslim League** was formed in the year **1906.**
 
• It was formed in **Dhaka, Bangladesh** during the British Raj.
 
• The main objective of the league was to protect the** political rights of Muslims** in India and to prevent their **marginalization **in the Hindu-dominated **Indian National Congress.**
 
• The league played a crucial role in the creation of **Pakistan in 1947,** which was a separate **Muslim-majority state **at the time of partition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indian National Congress** was formed in **1885** to represent the interests of the Indian people in the **British colonial government.**
 
• **1911 **is significant because it was the year when the **capital of British** India was shifted from** Calcutta to Delhi.**
 
• **1920 **is significant because it was the year when Mahatma Gandhi launched his** non-cooperation movement** against the British government, which was a major turning point in India's struggle for independence.

questions.question: Nadir Shah, ruler of Iran plundered the city of Delhi in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1739.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nadir Shah,** the ruler of Iran, invaded India in **1739 **and plundered the **city of Delhi.**
 
• This was a significant event in Indian history as it marked the** decline of the Mughal Empire **and the rise of **regional powers**.
 
• Nadir Shah's invasion was **brutal, **and he looted the city's riches, including the famous** Peacock Throne, **which was later taken to Iran.
 
• The invasion also resulted in the death of thousands of** civilians and soldiers,** and it took several years for **Delhi** to recover from the devastation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nadir Shah** was a powerful** ruler of Iran** and is considered one of the most **successful military commanders** of his time.
 
• He invaded India to plunder its riches and also to avenge the **defeat of his predecessor, Tahmasp II**, by the Mughals in the **Battle of Karnal.**
 
• Nadir Shah's invasion of India was one of the last major invasions by a** foreign power **and marked the beginning of the end of the Mughal Empire.
 
• The Peacock Throne, which Nadir Shah took from Delhi, was later seized by the **Afghan ruler Ahmad Shah Durrani **and eventually ended up in the possession of the** British East India Company.**
 
• The invasion of **Delhi by Ahmad Shah Durrani in 1761** was also a significant event in Indian history, as it led to the weakening of the Maratha Empire and paved the way for **British colonial rule.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a family in classification of Modern Indian Languages?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indo - African.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indo-African** is not a recognized family in the classification of **Modern Indian Languages.**
 
• The other options are recognized **language families in India.**
 
• **Indo-European** refers to languages like **Hindi, Bengali, and Punjabi**, while Sino-Tibetan refers to languages like **Tibetan and Burmese.**
 
• **Dravidian** refers to a language family that includes languages like **Tamil, Telugu, and Kannada**, and is one of the major language families in India.
 
• It is important to note that the classification of languages into families is based on** linguistic similarities and differences,** and can change over time as new research is conducted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The key word in the question is **"classification of Modern Indian Languages,"** which refers to the categorization of languages spoken in India based on **linguistic similarities and differences.**
 
• **Indo-European** is the largest language family in India, and includes many of the most widely spoken languages in the country.
 
 
• It is also spoken in many other parts of the world, including** Europe and parts of Asia.**
 
 
 
• **Sino-Tibetan** is a language family that is primarily spoken in** East Asia**, but also includes some languages spoken in India, like **Manipuri and Tibetan.**
 
• **Dravidian** is one of the major language families in India, and includes languages spoken primarily in** South India.**
 
 
• It is distinct from **Indo-European and Sino-Tibetan, **and has its own unique characteristics and features.

questions.question: The Brihadisvara temple at Tanjavur was constructed by ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajaraja I.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajaraja I **was a **Chola king** who ruled from **985 to 1014 CE.**
 
• He is known for his **military conquests, administrative reforms,** and **patronage of the arts.**
 
• The **Brihadisvara temple at Tanjavur,** also known as the Big Temple, is one of the finest examples of **Chola architecture.**
 
• It was built during **Rajaraja I's reign** and completed in **1010 CE.**
 
• The temple is dedicated to **Lord Shiva **and features a towering** vimana (tower) **that is over **200 feet tall.**
 
• It is adorned with **intricate carvings and sculptures** that depict scenes from **Hindu mythology.**
 
• The Brihadisvara temple is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** and attracts thousands of visitors every year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajendra I** was Rajaraja I's son and successor.

 
 
• He ruled from **1012 to 1044 CE** and continued his father's legacy of** military conquests and patronage of the arts.**
 
• He built the **Gangaikonda Cholapuram temple,** which is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Vijayalaya** was the founder of the** Chola dynasty **and ruled from **850 to 870 CE.**
 
 
• He established the capital at **Thanjavur** and built the first temple of the **Chola era there.**
 
 
 
• **Aditya I** was another Chola king who ruled from **871 to 907 CE**.
 
 
• He expanded the Chola empire and built several temples, including the** Thiruvellarai temple and the Thirukadaiyur temple.**

questions.question: Subsidiary Alliance was a system devised by _______ in 1798
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Wellesley.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Subsidiary Alliance** was a system introduced by **Lord Wellesley in 1798.**
 
• The system was devised as a means to **strengthen British power** in India and to** establish control** over the **princely states.**
 
• Under the system, the Indian ruler was required to **accept British protection and assistance** in return for ceding control of their **foreign affairs **and allowing British troops to be stationed in their territory.
 
• The system was also used as a means to **extract revenue** from the princely states and to prevent them from forming alliances with other** European powers.**
 
• Lord Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance system was a significant factor in the** consolidation of British power** in India and played a key role in the eventual establishment of British colonial rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Lord Bentinck** was the **Governor-General of India** from **1828 to 1835.**

 
 
• He is known for his social reforms, including **abolition of Sati and suppression of Thuggee.**
 
 
 
• **Lord Dalhousie **was the **Governor-General of India** from **1848 to 1856.**
 
 
• He is known for his policies of annexation, including the **annexation of Punjab, **and for introducing the **Doctrine of Lapse.**
 
 
 
• **Lord Hastings **was the **Governor-General of India** from **1813 to 1823.**
 
 
• He is known for his military campaigns against the** Marathas and the Pindaris.**

questions.question: Materials that allow electric current to pass through them are called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**conductors.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Conductors** are materials that **allow electric current** to pass through them easily, due to the **presence of free electrons** in their atomic structure.
 
• These electrons are not bound to any particular atom and can** move freely **within the material when a **voltage is applied.**
 
• Examples of common conductors include metals like **copper, aluminum, and silver**, as well as some **non-metals** like **graphite **(used in pencils) and **plasma **(found in lightning bolts and some types of lamps).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Insulators** are materials that **do not allow electric current **to flow through them easily.

 
 
• They have** few free electron**s and a** high resistance** to electrical flow.
 
• Examples include **rubber, glass, and most plastics. **
 
 
 
• **Alternators** are devices that **convert mechanical energy** (e.g. from an engine or turbine) into electrical energy, by using rotating magnets to induce a** current** in a stationary coil of wire.
 
 
• They are commonly used in **cars and power plants.**
 
 
 
• **Capacitors** are electronic components that** store electrical energy** in an electric field.
 
 
• They consist of **two conductive plates **separated by an insulating material (dielectric), and can be used in circuits for **filtering, timing, and energy storage.**

questions.question: ________ refers to sale and purchase of government securities by RBI in the open market with the aim of influencing liquidity in the economy in the medium term.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Open Market Operations.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Open Market Operations (OMO)** is a **monetary policy tool** used by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** to manage **liquidity **in the economy.
 
• Through OMO, the RBI **buys or sells government securities** in the open market, which influences the** money supply** in the economy.
 
• OMO can be used to inject liquidity into the system by** purchasing securities**, or to** absorb excess liquidity **by selling securities.
 
• OMO is considered a **medium-term tool** as its impact on liquidity takes a few weeks to materialize.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marginal Standing Facility (MSF)** is a short-term **borrowing** facility for banks.
 
• **Credit Ceiling** refers to a limit on the amount of credit that can be** extended** by banks.
 
• **Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF)** is a mechanism used by the RBI to manage **short-term liquidity** in the economy by adjusting the** repo rate and reverse repo rate.**
